crowdsourced_ai_results.analysis: This binary is a legitimate Microsoft Early Launch Anti-Malware (ELAM) kernel driver, likely part of Windows Defender or the Microsoft Malware Protection engine. Its primary functions include monitoring boot-start drivers using the IoRegisterBootDriverCallback and protecting critical system registry keys via CmRegisterCallback. The driver performs signature verification using the BCrypt API (SHA1/RSA) to ensure the integrity of loaded components. HLIL analysis reveals standard ELAM behavior, such as querying 'SystemStartOptions' for 'TESTSIGNING' mode and persisting anti-malware configuration data in the HKLM\ELAM registry hive. Internal function names like MpEbBootDriverCallback and WdBoot further confirm its identity as a standard Windows security component.
